renege

rih-NIG (rhymes with 'big') · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To renege is to go back on a promise or agreement.

Card players who renege on a bet without paying up quickly find themselves uninvited from future games.

Example

Voters felt betrayed when the mayor seemed poised to renege on his campaign pledge to lower property taxes.

To renege is to go back on your word after having committed to something, often disappointing people who trusted you.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

backpedal: To backpedal is to retreat from something you said -- softening, hedging, or reversing a stated position, the way a politician backpedals on a bold claim. To renege is more serious: you gave your word on a real commitment -- a promise, a bet, a deal -- and then broke it. Backpedaling undoes talk; reneging breaks a deal.

default: To default is to fail to meet an obligation, especially a payment -- often because the money simply is not there. To renege is a choice: you could keep your word, but you deliberately back out of it. Defaulting can come from an empty account; reneging comes from a change of heart.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

honor: to fulfill a promise or agreement

fulfill: to carry out or complete what was promised

Where it sits · how badly a commitment is broken — hesitate → renege → betray

hesitate vs. renege: To hesitate is only to pause and waver before acting -- someone who hesitates over a promise may still keep it, while someone who reneges has already broken it.

betray vs. renege: To betray someone is a deeper, more damaging breach of trust than simply reneging on one deal.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: back (Latin)

root — nege

root — nege: to deny (from Latin negare)

Put it together

Put it together: Renege is built from re- ('back') + nege ('to deny,' from Latin negare) -- literally 'to deny back,' which came to mean taking back your word after promising something.

Use the root in a new word: negate

Use the root in a new word: negate: One careless mistake can negate hours of careful preparation.

Root Check

Word Choice

Renege usually implies you had given your word -- a promise, a bet, a deal -- and then deliberately backed out of it. It's a more personal, informal cousin of repudiate (a formal, public rejection of a claim or belief) and rescind (an official cancellation of a law, contract, or policy).
